title: Prologue
content:
“Wei Wuxian is dead!Best news all year!”

The grand siege of the Burial Mounds had barely ended, yet before dawn could even break, the news spread like wildfire across the cultivation world—moving faster than the flames of war ever did.

From the most prestigious great clans down to rogue cultivators wandering the hinterlands, everyone had only one thing on their lips: the joint purge orchestrated by the Four Great Sects and backed by hundreds of lesser clans.

“Good, good! Truly music to my ears! So, which hero finally ran that Yiling Laozu through?”

“Who else? His own shidi, Sect Leader Jiang Cheng. The Four Great Clans—Yunmeng Jiang, Lanling Jin, Gusu Lan, and Qinghe Nie—led the charge. Pure righteousness over blood ties! They stormed Wei Wuxian’s viper’s nest at the Burial Mounds and wiped it off the face of the earth.”

“Let’s call a spade a spade: the bastard deserved it.”

A bystander clapped in hearty agreement. “Damn right he did! If the Yunmeng Jiang clan hadn’t taken him in and cultivated him, Wei Ying would’ve spent his whole life as some nobody scrounging through gutters. Forget all his grand airs—the late Sect Leader Jiang practically raised him as a son! And how did he repay them? Turned traitor, made enemies of the entire world, dragged the Jiang name through the dirt, and got nearly the whole family wiped out. If that’s not an ungrateful, venomous snake, I don’t know what is!”

“Jiang Cheng let that creature run wild for way too long. If it were up to me, I wouldn’t have just stabbed him back when he defected—I’d have cleaned house and finished him right then and there. Then he wouldn’t have lived long enough to commit all those unhinged atrocities later. Why bother with old courtesies like ‘childhood friends’ and ‘fellow disciples’ for scum like that?”

“Wait, but that’s not what I heard? Didn’t Wei Ying die from his own demonic cultivation backfiring? I heard his ghostly fiends turned on him and ripped him to shreds—literally chewed him down into powder.”

“Hahaha! That’s called karma! I’ve been saying it forever: the corpse-soldiers he kept were like rabid dogs without leashes, snapping at everyone. In the end, they mauled their own master to death. Serves him right!”

“Even so, if young Sect Leader Jiang hadn't devised a plan targeting the Yiling Laozu’s weaknesses, who knows if the siege would’ve worked at all? Don’t forget what kind of horrors Wei Wuxian had in his pocket. Remember how over three thousand renowned cultivators were annihilated in a single night?”

“Wasn't it five thousand?”

“Three, five—same difference. Honestly, five thousand sounds more like him.”

“Truly a lunatic…”

“At least he had the sense to destroy the Yin Tiger Tally before he kicked the bucket. If that ungodly thing were still around to wreak havoc on the living, his sins would be tenfold worse.”

At the mention of the Yin Tiger Tally, a sudden hush fell over the room, as if just speaking the name could summon a curse.

After a tense beat, someone let out a heavy sigh.

“Ah… you know, back in the day, that Wei Wuxian was genuinely one of the most brilliant young masters in the cultivation clans. He had plenty of legendary feats under his belt. Rising to fame so young, so arrogant, so free-spirited… How on earth did he fall this far?”

With the ice broken, the chatter flared up again.

“Just goes to show you: in cultivation, you stick to the orthodox path or you pay the price. Demonic arts might give you a moment of blinding glory, make you look untouchable, right? Heh, and where did that get him in the end?”

A cold, ringing verdict: “Not even a whole corpse left to bury!”

“It wasn’t just the demonic path that doomed him, though. At the end of the day, Wei Wuxian was rotten to the core. He stirred up heaven's wrath and man’s disgust. What goes around comes around—heaven keeps tabs on everyone.”

Death settled the score. The coffin was sealed, the verdict passed. The murmurs everywhere told the exact same tale, and any faint voice of dissent was smothered immediately.

Yet, a dark haze lingered over every heart, refusing to dissipate.

The Yiling Laozu, Wei Wuxian, had indeed perished on the Burial Mounds. But after the dust settled, not a single ritual could summon his shattered soul.

Perhaps his spirit had been torn apart and consumed alongside his flesh by the ravenous horde of ghosts. Or perhaps… it had slipped away.

If it were the former, everyone could rejoice with absolute peace of mind. But the Yiling Laozu had wielded power capable of upending heaven and earth—or so the rumors claimed. Shrugging off a soul-summoning would hardly be beyond him. And if his spiritual core ever reassembled, if he ever snatched a body to return from the dead… the clans, and indeed the entire mortal realm, would face a storm of vicious vengeance far darker and bloodier than before.

And so, after weighing down the peak of the Burial Mounds with one hundred and twenty spirit-warding stone beasts, the great clans began staging relentless soul-calling rites. At the same time, they launched strict crackdowns against body-snatching, tracked every regional oddity, and stayed on high alert.

The first year, calm and quiet.

The second year, peaceful as a breeze.

The third year, entirely still.

…

By the thirteenth year, not a single ripple had disturbed the water.

Finally, more and more people began to believe that maybe Wei Wuxian hadn’t been quite as omnipotent as they thought. Maybe his soul truly had been wiped from existence.

Even a man who once commanded the clouds and rain would eventually be overturned by the storm.

No one stays on an altar forever. A legend, in the end, is just a story told in the dark.
